content: Cefotetan is a sterile, semi-synthetic, broad-spectrum cephalosporin antibiotic that is resistant to beta-lactamase enzymes. It is intended for parenteral administration, either intravenously or intramuscularly. The active ingredient is cefotetan disodium, which is the disodium salt of a complex chemical structure: 7-[2-amino-2-(4-thiazolyl)acetamido]-7-methoxy-3-methyl-8-oxo-5-thia-1-azabicyclo[4.2.0]oct-2-ene-2-carboxylic acid. Each gram of cefotetan activity contains 57.5 mEq of sodium. Cefotetan appears as a white to pale yellow powder that is highly soluble in water. When reconstituted, the solutions are intended for intravenous or intramuscular use and may range in color from colorless to yellow, depending on the concentration. Cefotetan is available in two vial strengths: 1 g and 2 g. Each 1 g vial contains cefotetan disodium equivalent to 1 g of cefotetan activity, and each 2 g vial contains cefotetan disodium equivalent to 2 g of cefotetan activity. Cefotetan is also available in a premixed, frozen, iso-osmotic, sterile, and non-pyrogenic solution in Galaxy® plastic containers (PL 2040). These containers are available in 50 mL volumes containing either 1 g or 2 g of cefotetan as cefotetan disodium. Sodium bicarbonate is added to convert cefotetan free acid to its sodium salt form, and the pH may be adjusted with hydrochloric acid. Each gram of cefotetan activity in this formulation contains 57.5 mEq of sodium. After thawing to room temperature, the solution is intended for intravenous use only. The Galaxy® container is made from a specially designed multilayer plastic (PL 2040). The solution comes into contact with the polyethylene layer of the container, and small amounts of certain chemical components of the plastic may leach into the solution during the product's shelf life. However, the suitability of the plastic has been confirmed through animal testing in accordance with USP biological tests for plastic containers, as well as tissue culture toxicity studies.
